selected_news.title: NASA Space Apps Challenge 181.835 katılımla tarih yazdı
selected_news.summary: 2 min read NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records Two NASA Space Apps Challenge participants in Vilhena, Brazil work together during the annual hackathon on their project submission. NASA On Nov. 14 and 15, NASA held the annual Space Apps Challenge with a record-breaking 181,835 registered participants taking part in 593 events around the world. The annual hackathon invites participants to use NASA’s open data to address one of 14 challenges focused on space exploration or Earth science. This year, the hackathon drew 59% more registrants and was the 5th year in a row with increased participation. Since 2012, NASA Space Apps Challenge has hosted the two-day event, which has included more than 600,000 people from more than 190 countries. The challenge provides an opportunity for hands-on experience with NASA science, mobilizing an engaged global community of technologists and space science enthusiasts to answer questions that benefit humanity and drive exploration. Participants join events organized by local volunteers to work in teams and address one of the challenges and submit their project before the deadline. Projects are then judged to determine 10 global winners, to be announced in January. “The Space Apps Challenge invites people with many different skillsets to leverage NASA’s gold-standard datasets to address real challenges facing us here on Earth and in space,” said Amy Kaminski, engagement branch chief, Science Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters in Washington. “We’re thrilled to see more than 180,000 people tackling these challenges and helping to accelerate our ability to find solutions.” One of the local winning teams from NASA Space Apps Challenge NYC pose with volunteer local lead Nate Cooper. NASA Challenges also feature data from 17 international space agency partners, all Artemis Accord signatories. This year’s space agency partners are: Angola National Space Programme Management Office (GGPEN), Bahrain Space Agency, Brazilian Space Agency (AEB), CSA (Canadian Space Agency), ESA (European Space Agency), ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation), Italian Space Agency, JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency), KASA (Korea AeroSpace Administration), Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Center of the United Arab Emirates, National Space Activities Commission of Argentina (CONAE), Nigeria’s National Space Research and Development Agency, Paraguayan Space Agency, Senegalese Space Studies Agency, Spanish Space Agency, Turkish Space Agency, and UK Space Agency. Three agencies, GGPEN, AEB, and CONAE, also wrote challenges this year. To learn more about NASA’s Space Apps Challenge, visit: spaceappschallenge.org Karen Fox / Jessica Hall Headquarters, Washington karen.c.fox@nasa.gov / jessica.hall@nasa.gov Share Details Last Updated Nov 17, 2026 Related Terms Open Science Explore More 4 min read NASA Welcomes All Ages, Experience Levels for Space Apps Challenge Article 1 month ago 4 min read NASA’s Prithvi Becomes First AI Geospatial Foundation Model In Orbit A team of researchers demonstrated NASA and IBM’s open-source Prithvi Geospatial artificial intelligence foundation model… Article 6 months ago 5 min read How Open NASA Data on Comet 3I/ATLAS Will Power Tomorrow’s Discoveries Article 8 months ago Keep Exploring Discover Related Topics Missions Humans in Space Climate Change Solar System

selected_news.title: Bangladeş ve Türkiye, Yenilenebilir Enerjide Yeni İş Birliği
selected_news.summary: Minister urges closer Bangladesh-Türkiye ties on energy, humanitarian affairs | Daily Sabah Daily Sabah
selected_news.query: Middle East latest news diplomacy humanitarian
selected_news.source_headline: Minister urges closer Bangladesh-Türkiye ties on energy, humanitarian affairs
selected_news.article_text: Türkiye and Bangladesh have maintained strong relations for decades despite the geographical distance between them. However, in recent years, their bilateral ties have begun to take on a new dimension. Shama Obaed Islam, Bangladesh’s state minister for foreign affairs, said that relations have improved further since the government took office in February. Highlighting Türkiye’s positive role in strengthening bilateral relations, Islam thanked President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and the Justice and Development Party (AK Party) government. "We appreciate Türkiye’s offer to cooperate with us in knowledge-sharing, technology transfer and energy production,” Islam told Daily Sabah in an exclusive interview during the COP31 climate summit last week. Stressing that Bangladesh aims to expand cooperation with Türkiye in the field of renewable energy, Islam said the country has embarked on an energy transition nationwide through solar panels and rooftop solar systems. “We feel that we can benefit from Türkiye’s experience,” Islam said, noting that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman aims to leave a clean country for future generations in Bangladesh. According to the Turkish Foreign Ministry, Türkiye and Bangladesh had agreed to step up cooperation in renewable energy during bilateral talks in October 2025. Türkiye’s expertise in green technologies and Bangladesh’s growing demand for diversified and sustainable energy solutions were emphasized. After the new government was established in Bangladesh, a series of bilateral meetings took place in recent months. The two countries reiterated their interest in exploring potential cooperation not only in renewable energy but also in nuclear energy and onshore and offshore hydrocarbon exploration, under a win-win approach. Türkiye is also considering providing technical expertise, investment and renewable energy technologies to support Bangladesh’s efforts to diversify its energy sources. Islam said Bangladesh’s government was also keen to explore new initiatives and was closely following the Zero Waste Initiative spearheaded by Türkiye’s first lady, Emine Erdoğan. Referring to meetings on the Zero Waste Initiative, Islam said, “The prime minister’s wife, Zubaida Rahman, had a meeting with Mrs. Erdoğan, where we discussed how we could generate energy from waste.” Drawing attention to the impact of the climate crisis, particularly on vulnerable communities, Islam said women and children were among the groups most severely affected by climate-related disasters. “So whenever there are disasters caused by climate change, women and children are the most vulnerable groups,” she said. Islam emphasized the importance of bringing women into education and professional life to promote women's empowerment. Türkiye and Bangladesh could grow together by sharing their knowledge and experiences in these areas, she noted. Islam also identified the refugee crisis as another key humanitarian concern shared by Türkiye and Bangladesh, emphasizing Dhaka’s sensitivity to the issue. “We have more than 1.3 million Rohingya who have been in Bangladesh for the past 10 years,” Islam said, adding, “We want the Rohingya community to return to their homeland with dignity.” Islam stressed that Bangladesh needed international support to resolve the Rohingya crisis. As of November 2026, Bangladesh remains among the world's largest host countries for refugees. According to a 2026 United Nations report, women and children make up more than half of the Rohingya refugee population. Meanwhile, UNICEF reported that approximately 34% of Rohingya children between ages 5 and 18 lacked access to learning opportunities supported by the education sector. Türkiye, on the other hand, has been hosting Syrian refugees since April 2011 under a temporary protection framework. According to Turkish ministry reports, the Syrian refugee population peaked at more than 3 million in 2022. UNHCR reported that around 755,000 Syrians had returned since December 2024, as of September 2026. Noting that Bangladesh and Türkiye were not the only countries facing such challenges, Islam pointed out that humanitarian and refugee crises, conflicts and wars were unfolding in different parts of the world. “So, globally, whether it is Gaza, Ukraine, the Gulf or our Rohingya refugee crisis, the world needs to unite to stop wars,” she said, calling for greater international cooperation to bring conflicts to an end

selected_news.title: Avrupa Mahkemesi Atalay’ın Serbest Bırakılmasını Emretti
selected_news.summary: The European Court of Human Rights has called for the release of imprisoned elected lawmaker Can Atalay. Atalay has been in prison for almost five years despite rulings from the Turkish Constitutional Court.
selected_news.source_headline: Rights court rules Turkey must release jailed lawmaker Atalay
selected_news.article_text: The European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) ruled against Turkey over the detention of human rights lawyer and elected lawmaker Can Atalay The ECHR published its decision on Tuesday, saying that Turkey must release Atalay and allow him to take up his seat in the Turkish parliament The court ruled that his continued detention had been intended to silence him and undermine political pluralism It ordered Turkey to pay him €32,500 (about $35,700) in compensation The judges stressed that Atalay's case should not be considered separately, but rather in the wider context of the detention of political opponents, human rights activists and journalists in Turkey To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Turkey was among the original signatories of the European Convention on Human Rights. Yet it has previously refused to comply with the court's decisions in the cases of rights activist Osman Kavala and prominent Kurdish politician Selahattin Demirtas As a lawyer, Atalay represented victims in numerous social and political cases in Turkey, as well as in freedom of speech cases involving journalists and writers He was also among the leading voices in the 2013 Gezi protests, which the government called an attempted coup Because of his involvement in the protests, Atalay, along with seven others, was sentenced to 18 years in prison in April 2022 for "aiding and abetting an attempted coup." Continuing his struggle from the infamous Silivri prison, Atalay ran as a candidate for the Workers' Party of Turkey (TIP) in the 2023 parliamentary elections To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video A candidate for the earthquake-hit province of Hatay, he won his seat but was denied release despite multiple rulings by the Constitutional Court, Turkey's top court His parliamentary status was revoked in 2024, a decision the Constitutional Court later overturned. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's party stopped the opposition from formally reading the decision in parliament Although a year later an opposition lawmaker read the decision in parliament, Atalay remains in jail After the ECHR's ruling was published, TIP leader Erkan Bas took to social media to call for Atalay's release and the restoration of his parliamentary mandate To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
